rules.statement: When a public method decodes or encodes into a caller-supplied `Span<byte>` destination, also provide an overload that writes to an `IBufferWriter<byte>` (generic `TWriter : IBufferWriter<byte>, allows ref struct` passed by `ref`), with a matching `GetByteCount` sizing method.
rules.why: The maintainer asked for a buffer-writer overload next to the span-only decode API so callers don't have to size and rent buffers themselves. The writer form follows the shared writer-overload shape, with `GetByteCount` as its sizing method.
rules.check: Look for new public methods that take a `Span<byte>` destination and return the number of bytes written, such as Decode, Encode or Write. Flag any that has no `IBufferWriter<byte>` overload alongside it.

rules.statement: In an `IBufferWriter<byte>` overload that decodes or parses input, validate the whole input before calling `GetSpan`/`GetMemory` or `Advance` on the writer, so that malformed input throws without advancing the writer.
rules.why: If invalid input throws after the writer has been advanced, the caller's writer is left holding partial output. Validating first keeps the writer unchanged when an error occurs.
rules.check: In writer-based decode methods, check whether the code can request or advance the writer's buffer before the input is fully validated. Also check whether it can throw after `Advance` has been called.
